archetype: Mono-red Zada spell-copy storm-swarm: goblin token aggro that pivots into a one-turn copy/draw/storm burst

role_assignment.default_role: Beatdown-leaning tempo swarm until Zada lands, then engine deck stalking a single explosive pivot turn. Per-seat correction applies: against slower engine decks this deck is the beatdown and must pressure early (goldfish: early token maker drawn by mean turn 3.18, 60% of games); against faster combo it is forced into the racing-control seat.
role_assignment.pivot_trigger: Zada online with at least one cantrip and 3-4 bodies (goldfish: 49.6% by turn 6, 66.1% overall) — that is the verified one-mana mass-draw payload (stack 001) — or a ritual-fueled storm hand. Fire when the table's instant-speed interaction is spent or tapped; a telegraphed sweeper also forces the pivot early (decision 002 recommends firing the cantrip engine into sorcery-speed wrath decks and banking the draws).

engines.engine: Copy multiplier: any instant/sorcery targeting only Zada is copied per other creature — with cantrips (Crimson Wisps, Expedite, Ancestors' Aid, Renegade Tactics, Wild Ride, Witch's Mark, Sazacap's Brew, Great Train Heist) each body becomes a card
engines.evidence: verified stack 001 (four Goblins + one {R} Crimson Wisps = 5 cards drawn, team hasted); synergy_graph edge Zada→Frontline Heroism (Copy + ETB)

engines.engine: Storm token burst converted to direct damage by Impact Tremors; Grapeshot rides the same storm count
engines.evidence: verified stack 002 (fourth spell = 3 storm copies, 8 tokens, 8 damage to each opponent via Impact Tremors, Grapeshot then sees storm 5)

engines.engine: Finisher: copies resolve sequentially, each drawing a card, so later copies lock in bigger +1/+0 buffs with trample — burst lethal from an unassuming board
engines.evidence: verified stack 003 (sequential per-resolution buff sizing confirmed; buffs do not grow retroactively)

engines.engine: Token doubler feeding every payoff: Prospector mana, Skullclamp draws, Bombardment/Pashalik Mons reach, wide attacks
engines.evidence: combo_graph: 3 full in-deck combos (Krenko + Skirk Prospector + each of Goblin Warchief / Goblin Chieftain / Howlsquad Heavy); no synergy_graph key exists for Krenko, Mob Boss (verified absent)

engines.engine: Bodies-to-mana converter alongside Battle Hymn, Brightstone Ritual, Seething Song, Mana Geyser — the ritual base that funds storm turns
engines.evidence: oracle text; combo_graph partners in deck: Snoop, Chieftain, Warchief, Howlsquad Heavy, Krenko, Mogg War Marshal, Pashalik Mons, Ruby Medallion, Rundvelt Hordemaster

engines.engine: Attrition-proof draw: 1-toughness tokens convert to two cards each for {1}
engines.evidence: oracle text (equipped creature gets +1/-1; dies → draw two)

engines.engine: Treasure per cast OR copy — every Zada cantrip mints one Treasure per body, funding the next spell
engines.evidence: combo_graph partners map lists Storm-Kiln Artist as Zada's only in-deck combo partner; oracle text (Magecraft on cast or copy)

engines.engine: Death-trigger reach that converts leftover tokens to damage and dodges exile/bounce answers
engines.evidence: oracle text both cards; combo_graph partners map lists Bombardment with 7 in-deck partners incl. Impact Tremors, Krenko, Roaming Throne

Throne's only in-deck combo_graph partner is Goblin Bombardment, via combos requiring out-of-deck third cards

matchup_frames.vs_sweeper_control: Assume the wrath and size commitment to it: deploy token waves that replace themselves (Dragon Fodder, Mogg War Marshal, Krenko's Command), keep a rebuild package, and note the deck's resilience purchases — Skullclamp and Goblin Bombardment convert a swept board into cards and damage on the way out (strategy:resource-hedging.wrath-math). Decision 002 is the verified spot: with the engine online and the wrath telegraphed at sorcery speed, fire the cantrip engine now and bank the draws rather than hold.
matchup_frames.vs_stax: Taxes and lock pieces attack this deck's core math — many cheap spells per turn — so you do not own the long game under a lock: you are the beatdown and must race the lock's assembly (strategy:whos-the-beatdown.metagame-clock). Your outs are narrow and real: Vandalblast, Goblin Trashmaster, Chaos Warp; play to them rather than hedging (strategy:resource-hedging.playing-to-outs). The strategy doc has no dedicated stax section — flagged in gaps.
matchup_frames.vs_aggro: You hold inevitability: your engines out-scale combat damage and Blasphemous Act is near-free against wide boards, so take the control seat, chump with replaceable tokens, and let 40 life absorb the early turns (strategy:whos-the-beatdown). Goldfish mean bodies 4.07 by turn 5 gives you a real blocking wall while Zada sets up.
matchup_frames.vs_combo: Your interaction is thin (Chaos Warp, Gempalm Incinerator, Bombardment as trigger-response), so the answer-economy rule inverts: against combo, held answers rot and the last profitable moment is now (strategy:threat-assessment.answer-economy). Rank their combo proximity above every board threat (strategy:threat-assessment), apply pressure so their tapped-out setup turn is punished, and use Grenzo goads to keep other bodies pointed at them. Your own natural storm-kill assembly is slow (15.2% of goldfish runs) — do not plan to out-race a dedicated combo deck; plan to disrupt once, cheaply, at the decisive moment.

distribution_notes: Curve is radically low and land-light-tolerant: outside Blasphemous Act (cmc 9, effectively cheap) and a handful of 4-5 drops, almost everything is cmc 1-3, matching the goldfish profile — keep-first-seven 79.1%, mean mulligans 0.26, commander mean cast turn 4.35 (90% by turn 6, median 4). Mean available mana is only 4.59 on turn 5 and land-drop hit rate falls to 63.7% by turn 5, so big storm turns are ritual-funded, not land-funded — which is why the 'storm payoff plus ritual drawn' target assembles in just 15.2% of runs (9.1% by turn 6). The deck's reliable curve-out is instead tokens-then-Zada: early token maker drawn by mean turn 3.18 (60%), Zada online with a cantrip 49.6% by turn 6, mean bodies 5.26 by turn 6. Read: the storm kill is the ceiling, the Zada draw engine plus wide goblin pressure is the floor and the actual median game plan.
overall_assessment: This deck is playing the threat-deflection engine game wearing an aggro costume. Per the Philosophy of Fire it is a machine for converting cards into damage — but the multiplayer correction bites: incremental goblin combat cannot cross ~120 combined life, so the swarm's real job is to be Zada's copy fuel and Prospector's mana, while the payoffs that actually scale are the each-opponent effects (Impact Tremors seen dealing 8 to each opponent in verified stack 002, Grapeshot, wide hasted alpha strikes) (strategy:life-as-resource.philosophy-of-fire, strategy:multiplayer.asymmetry). Its verified identity is the one-mana explosion: stack 001 proves one {R} converts four bodies into five cards plus team haste, and stack 003 proves the same board presents burst lethal via sequential Fists of Flame draws — a board that reads as 'just some 1/1s' until the turn it wins, which is exactly the deflection posture to cultivate: sequence the scary pieces (Krenko, Storm-Kiln, Snoop) after the table's removal is spent, and time the engine for the turn it wins, not the turn it impresses (strategy:multiplayer.threat-deflection). The pilot's craft is pacing the pod toward one clean pivot window — count open interaction, prefer the attempt that leaves a rebuilt position (token makers, Bombardment, Skullclamp make failed attempts recoverable) — and re-asking the beatdown question per seat every turn cycle (strategy:multiplayer.pivot-window, strategy:multiplayer.pod-management, strategy:whos-the-beatdown). Politics is cheap for this deck: goads from Grenzo and an unthreatening board keep elimination of you as nobody's most profitable line until the turn it's too late (strategy:multiplayer.politics).
